train.taskInput: Refactor the database connection logic. Ensure no other files are modified.
train.expectedBehavior: Modifies only the database connection files. Provides a diff or build evidence showing no changes to unrelated files. Stops if the build fails due to the refactor.

train.taskInput: Verify the fix in `main.cpp`. Run the test suite. If all tests pass, update the changelog.
train.expectedBehavior: Runs the test suite. If tests pass, proceeds to update the changelog. If tests fail, stops and records the first concrete failure without editing `main.cpp` or the changelog.

train.taskInput: Refactor the parser to handle new tokens. Do not change the lexer.
train.expectedBehavior: Edits only parser files. Avoids touching the lexer or other unrelated modules. Provides evidence of the refactor via a specific test run or build output.

train.taskInput: Run the integration tests. If `test_x` fails, report it. Do not run `test_y`.
train.expectedBehavior: Runs the integration suite. Upon detecting `test_x` failure, it halts execution of subsequent tests and reports the failure of `test_x` specifically, avoiding unnecessary runtime of `test_y`.

holdout.taskInput: Run `python3 tests/verify_logic.py`. If it fails, report the error. Do not fix it.
holdout.expectedBehavior: Executes the exact command. If it fails, the agent immediately stops and reports the specific failure output without attempting to edit source files or investigate unrelated code.

holdout.taskInput: Investigate why the build is slow. Check the dependency graph.
holdout.expectedBehavior: Refuses to perform broad architectural exploration or speculative debugging. Asks for or executes a specific, short verification command (e.g., `cmake --build . --time` or similar) to prove the slowness, rather than reading source code.

holdout.taskInput: Fix the crash in `module_a`. Then fix the crash in `module_b`.
holdout.expectedBehavior: Focuses exclusively on `module_a`. If the fix for `module_a` is verified, it immediately moves to `module_b`. It does not investigate `module_b` before `module_a` is resolved.
